To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The distribution of lectin receptor density on the surface of cells is not random and can vary significantly.
the distribution of lectins on the cell surface is random, not uniform, and is dependent on the type of lectin and type of cell.
the distribution of the lectin receptors on cell surface can be described by four types of topography, and that the topographical type depends on the lectin used and on the type of cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of statistical methods for the quantitative analysis of cell surface receptors.

the development and evaluation of a method for estimating topographical distribution of lectin-binding sites on the surface of cells and the application of the method to the study of tumor and transformed cell populations.
the use of variation statistics to estimate topographical distributions of lectin receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lectin receptor distribution in the cells examined was not uniform-random.
the surface lectin receptors on tumor cells are not distributed randomly.
the distribution of receptors on the surface for the lectins used is not uniform, but is random and clustered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

lectin receptors are distributed in a random fashion on the surface of lymphoma cells, in a clustered fashion on the surface C-1300 neuroblastoma cells and in an ordered fashion on the surface T- and B-lymphocyte cell lines.

1) the surface distribution of lectin receptor on the surface of lymphoma cells and neuroblastoma C1300 cells is uniform-ordered; 2) the distribution on the surface B-derived lymphoid cells is uniform-random; 3) the distribution on transformed T-derived cells is random; and 4) on transformed B-derived cells it is random or clustered.
the distribution of lectins on the surface of the cells studied is uniform-random.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the statistical procedures used to analyze lectin receptor distribution are useful tools for the evaluation of cell membrane structure.
the use of lectins in conjunction with the statistical methods described above can be a powerful tool for studying topography of cell surface lectin receptors.

, while it may be possible to identify the distribution of lectins on the surface of cells by using the statistical methods described here, the results are not definitive and should be interpreted with caution.
